name: The Skyline Club
note: You step out of the lift into moving air and the sound of a room that started without you.

arts.name: The Water
arts.desc: The pool is four feet deep and nobody has ever swum in it. It exists to put moving light on the faces of people having conversations near it, which it does exceptionally well.

arts.name: The Parapet
arts.desc: The glass edge. Every significant conversation on this roof has happened within six feet of it, because people tell the truth more readily when they can see how far down it is.

arts.name: The Cabanas
arts.desc: Four of them. Three can be booked. The fourth has never been available on any night, to anyone, and the staff have been trained not to explain why.

arts.name: The Corner Booth
arts.desc: Faces the door, backs to the wall, worst view in the building. Held permanently. If you are sitting in it you were invited to sit in it.

name: The Living Room
note: Two storeys of it, and somebody was sitting here twenty minutes ago. The glass is still cold.

arts.name: The Journal
arts.desc: Left face-down and open, which he knows ruins a spine. Everything written in it eventually turns up here, several drafts later — dispatches, not diary entries.

arts.name: The Piano
arts.desc: He played trumpet for seven years, first chair, and cannot play this at all. It is here because a room with a piano in it behaves differently from a room without one — and because it's wired to whatever he's actually listening to.

arts.name: The Vault
arts.desc: Brass wheel, black steel, set into the wall beside the piano and not hidden behind anything. A safe nobody can see is a safe somebody goes looking for. What's inside isn't paper.

arts.name: The Candle
arts.desc: Unlit, on the back counter, waiting on a launch date nobody will confirm yet. UR Welcome — coming soon.

arts.name: The Jacket
arts.desc: Left over the back of the reading chair rather than hung, which tells you he wasn't planning on staying gone long. Everything else he owns is arranged by occasion — see the Boutique.

name: The Bedroom
note: Blackout to the glass, and a bed that faces away from the view on purpose.

arts.name: The Artwork
arts.desc: Bought a long time before he could afford it, and hung on every wall he has had since. A man on a road at dusk, walking away from whatever the painter could not be bothered to explain. It hangs behind the headboard, so he only sees it when he turns around.

arts.name: The Lounge Chair
arts.desc: Angled at the window rather than the television, because there is no television. Most of the thinking that matters happens in it.

arts.name: The Closet Door
arts.desc: Left open more often than not. What is behind it is arranged by occasion, not by colour — see the Closet.

name: The Bathroom
note: Stone, brass and steam, with the whole city on the other side of the glass.

name: The Closet
note: Not a room of clothes. A room of decisions already made.

arts.name: The Suits & Tuxedos
arts.desc: Arranged by occasion rather than colour, so getting dressed is a question of where you are going rather than what you feel like. Two dinner jackets at the centre, black-tie and white-tie, either one pressed and ready before he has to ask.

arts.name: The Shoes
arts.desc: Cedar-treed, rotated, never worn two days running. The oldest pair on the shelf is fourteen years old and still the best thing in the room.

arts.name: The Ties
arts.desc: Hung rather than rolled. He owns more than he wears and knows it, and has stopped pretending that will change.

name: The Kitchen
note: Black marble, brass, and one box that showed up on the counter this morning.

arts.name: The Delivery
arts.desc: It arrived before he did. No note, no ceremony — just the box, already unpacked onto the marble like it had always been there. He does not cook often. He cooks well when he does, and never asks how the box knew that.

name: The Study
note: The room where the answer is usually no, and where it gets said politely.

arts.name: The Monogram
arts.desc: Brass, wall-mounted, deliberately the only branded object in the entire apartment. He is aware of the contradiction and finds it funny.

arts.name: The Pullen Laws
arts.desc: Fourteen of them, on the left-hand shelf, written down over eleven years because a rule you have to remember is a rule you will eventually forget. The first one is about arriving early. The fourteenth has never been read aloud.

arts.name: The Journal
arts.desc: This week's pages, face-up on the blotter for once, marked in pencil rather than ink so that nothing is decided yet. What survives the pencil goes out as a dispatch. Most of it does not survive the pencil.

arts.name: The Cocktail Guide
arts.desc: Six drinks, written on a card and kept behind the bottles, because a man looking up an Old Fashioned in front of guests has already lost the evening. Six is the entire list. There has never been a seventh.

arts.name: The Map
arts.desc: Brass inlay on black. Cities he has worked, not cities he has visited — a distinction he will make if you ask.

name: The Cinema
note: Nine seats, one screen, and a rule about phones that is actually enforced.

arts.name: The Posters
arts.desc: All one register: men in tailoring, making decisions, usually badly. He will tell you it is research. It is partly research.

name: The Corridor
note: No numbers on these doors. The carpet is thicker here, which is not a decorating choice.

arts.name: The Unmarked Door
arts.desc: There is no handle on this side. It opens from within, or it does not open. Staff are instructed never to knock on it, and never to mention it to a guest who has not mentioned it first.

arts.name: The Carpet
arts.desc: Deeper pile than the floors above and below. Sound does not carry in this hallway, and that is the entire specification.

arts.name: The Second Lift
arts.desc: It does not appear on the panel in the main bank. It is called by a card, not a button, and it only travels between three floors.

arts.name: The Weekly Delivery
arts.desc: It comes up the private line, not the guest elevator — the only recurring thing that does. The staff know not to ask what's inside. It's produce.

name: The Order
note: Twelve chairs. Eleven are spoken for. Nobody sits down until the last person is standing.

arts.name: The Twelfth Chair
arts.desc: Identical to the other eleven and never once occupied. It is not reserved for anyone. It is there so that everybody seated can see that the table is not full.

arts.name: The Table
arts.desc: One piece of walnut, brought in before the walls were finished because it does not fit through the door. The room was built around it, which is the point being made.

arts.name: The Lamps
arts.desc: Hung low enough that everyone's face is lit and nobody's eyes are in shadow. You cannot lie comfortably at this table. That is engineering, not decor.

name: The Operations Room
note: The warmest room in the building, and the only one where the furniture is doing arithmetic.

arts.name: The Table
arts.desc: Walnut with smoked glass inlaid flush into the surface, lit from beneath in fine amber linework. It shows the city as relationships rather than streets. At rest it is a very good table.

arts.name: The Instruments
arts.desc: Machined brass and titanium, laid out like surgical tools. None of them have a screen. Every one of them does something a screen would do worse.

arts.name: The Shelves
arts.desc: Real books, read. The technology in this room is deliberately outnumbered by things made of paper, which is a decision he will defend at length if asked.

name: The Lab
note: It smells like the inside of a cigar box and faintly of citrus. This is where the whole thing started.

arts.name: The Scales
arts.desc: Accurate to a hundredth of a gram. Everything else in the building is measured in impressions and relationships. This is the one room that deals in numbers that cannot be argued with.

arts.name: The Blotters
arts.desc: Fanned in a brass rack, each one a version that did not make it. She keeps them. He has asked why. She has not answered.

arts.name: The Notebook
arts.desc: Leather, handwritten, and the only complete formula record in existence. There is no digital copy, on purpose, and it does not leave this room.

arts.name: The Unlabelled Bottles
arts.desc: Amber glass, no labels, arranged in an order that makes sense to exactly one person. Moving them is the fastest way to be asked to leave.

name: The Haberdashery
note: Warm wood, cold discipline. The room where the building decides what you are going to look like.

arts.name: The Cloth Wall
arts.desc: Bolts stacked by weight, not colour. A client who asks for the blue one is gently redirected. A client who asks what will still look correct in nine years is offered a chair.

arts.name: The Cutting Table
arts.desc: Chalk, shears and forty years of hands. Nothing is cut on this table that has not been argued about first.

arts.name: The Shoes
arts.desc: A rack of them, all dark, all polished past the point of necessity. The first thing the doorman checks and the last thing an amateur thinks about.

arts.name: The Panel That Is Not A Panel
arts.desc: Third panel from the corner. It reads as joinery. It is a door, and behind it the room is not about tailoring.

name: The Armoury
note: A gentleman's defensive kit, in the Savile Row tradition. Nothing in here fires anything.

arts.name: The Umbrellas
arts.desc: Storm-rated, reinforced along the spine, weighted correctly for the hand. It rains a great deal in this state and a man should not be caught holding something flimsy.

arts.name: The Canes
arts.desc: Malacca and blackthorn. Two of them belonged to men who are named on the wall downstairs. They are carried on occasions that call for being reminded of something.

arts.name: The Sabres
arts.desc: Fencing blades, buttoned, kept sharp enough to be respected and blunt enough to be legal. He fences badly and enjoys it enormously.

arts.name: The Locked Case
arts.desc: The only locked thing in the building. It contains correspondence, not hardware, which is the joke and also the truth.

name: The Fitting Floor
note: Three mirrors, angled so you cannot avoid yourself. Somebody is mid-fitting. He does not stop.

arts.name: The Three Mirrors
arts.desc: Set so that you see your own back. Most men have never seen how they actually stand, and the first fitting is largely about surviving that information.

arts.name: The Rails
arts.desc: Finished garments waiting on brass. Each one has a name on the ticket and a date, and the date is when it was promised rather than when it was finished.

arts.name: The Cuff
arts.desc: Half an inch of shirt, no more. He adjusts it without thinking about it roughly forty times a day, which the Cutter finds funny and has never mentioned.

name: The Restaurant
note: Sixty covers, one seating, and a kitchen that closes when it is finished rather than when the clock says so.

arts.name: The Corner Table
arts.desc: Two chairs, both facing out. Every deal this building has ever done was either agreed at this table or fell apart at it.

arts.name: The Pass
arts.desc: Visible from the room on purpose. Diners can watch the kitchen work, and the kitchen can watch who has arrived, which matters more than the diners realise.

arts.name: The Arrangements
arts.desc: Replaced entirely twice a week, dark and slightly overgrown rather than neat. Neat flowers make a room look like it is trying.

name: The Bar
note: Low ceiling, low light, low voices. The best-run room in the building and the one he is proudest of.

arts.name: The Back Bar
arts.desc: Lit from within, unlabelled by house policy. If you want to know what you are drinking you have to ask, and asking is how conversations start.

arts.name: The Ice
arts.desc: Cut from a single block each afternoon. Clear ice melts slower, dilutes less, and signals that somebody spent time on your drink before you ordered it.

arts.name: The Brass Rail
arts.desc: Unlacquered, so it takes a fingerprint and keeps it. Polished once a week, never more, because a rail with no wear on it means nobody is standing here.

arts.name: The Banquettes
arts.desc: Burgundy leather, deliberately slightly too deep, so that people sit back rather than forward. Nobody has ever had a rushed conversation in one.

name: The Coffee House
note: The same marble counter, twelve hours earlier. Different room entirely.

arts.name: The Counter
arts.desc: This is the bar. At six in the morning the bottles are shuttered, the lights come up, and the same stone serves espresso to people who have no idea what happens here after dark.

arts.name: The Regulars
arts.desc: Bankers at six, builders at seven, the Cutter at eight-fifteen without fail. He orders the same thing and has never once said thank you, which everyone finds endearing.

arts.name: The Window
arts.desc: Ground floor, full height, facing the street. The only room in the building where the public can see in — and the only floor where that is the entire idea.

name: The Lobby
note: The doors give, the noise of the street stops, and the building tells you everything about itself in about four seconds.

arts.name: The Doors
arts.desc: Brass, and heavier than they need to be. The weight is the point — you have to commit to opening them, and by the time you are through you have already made a small decision about being here.

arts.name: The Arrangements
arts.desc: Replaced entirely twice a week and never symmetrical. They are cut tall enough that you cannot see the whole room at once, so the lobby reveals itself in pieces rather than all at once.

arts.name: The Water
arts.desc: A still black basin, no fountain, no movement. It exists so the room has a sound floor — the faint hush that stops a marble hall from ringing like a bank.

arts.name: The Desk
arts.desc: Honed black marble, no computer visible, no queue rope, no signage. Whoever is standing behind it already knows your name or is about to find it out.

arts.name: The Ceiling
arts.desc: Four storeys of it. Every material expense in this building was argued about except this one — height is the only luxury that cannot be faked, and he paid for it without discussion.

name: The Motor Club
note: Cool air, polished concrete, and twenty-four reasons somebody had a good year.

arts.name: The Bays
arts.desc: Twenty-four, each lit like an exhibit. The Curator can tell you what closed the deal that paid for every single one, and will, at length, if you make eye contact.

arts.name: The Lounge
arts.desc: At the far end, behind glass, so members can sit with a drink and look at the collection. Nobody has ever sat facing away from it.

arts.name: The Private Lift
arts.desc: Goes up. Does not stop at the lobby, the bar or the restaurant. There is only one card that calls it from down here.

name: The Inventory
note: Below the club. Colder, darker, and considerably more interesting.

arts.name: The Racks
arts.desc: Parts, panels and things that no longer exist anywhere else. When a car upstairs needs something unobtainable, it is obtained from down here.

arts.name: The Ledger
arts.desc: A handwritten record of every acquisition, what was paid, and who was outbid. That last column is the one people ask about and the one that never gets shown.

arts.name: The Crates
arts.desc: Unopened. Some for years. He buys things he does not need in order to be the person who has them when somebody finally does need one.
